title: No subcommand to append a new step mid-phase
context: `state.py append-record steps.json '{...}'` exists (covers PLAN-time and in principle mid-phase). The original framing was specifically about EXECUTE-time step creation; `instructions/execute.md` still funnels deferred work through devlog `Deferred:` flags so PLAN owns step authoring. If a real workflow demands runtime step append from EXECUTE, lift the restriction in execute.md prose - the CLI now supports it.
trigger: Phase 2 pilot shows execute-time step append is wanted; loosen the prose.
resolution: No occurrence. Steps sit below the executing model cognitive limit (no ask-too-large failures); discovered/extra work is handled by devlog `Deferred:` -> PLAN re-authors, so EXECUTE never needs to append a step. PLAN-owns-steps is a deliberate guardrail. (Occasional long / calls-limit steps are a step-sizing + multi-iteration-budget concern, i.e. Phase 3.C -- not this.) Reopen only if a real workflow proves EXECUTE-time step append is needed.

title: `state.py set` only handles JSON object files, not arrays
context: `update-record` (added for review/close authoring) covers single-record updates on array files via `--match KEY=VALUE`. Generic-set-on-array still isn't supported (e.g., updating fields on N records at once).
trigger: A real workflow needs bulk update across multiple records (rare). Until then, `update-record` covers the gap that drove FU-3 in practice.
resolution: Practical gap -- updating fields on array-file records -- is covered by `update-record` (single record, matched by KEY=VALUE); `set` did not need extending. Only unbuilt remainder is bulk update across N records at once: no occurrence, scriptable as a loop of `update-record` calls; file fresh if ever needed.

title: No named lifecycle-transition op (e.g., `state.py escalate --reason "..."`)
context: Post-FU-30 the `blocked` field is gone; lifecycle transitions use `state.py set project.json state=<enum>`. The dense `set` syntax works for autonomous and supervised use alike. A named op like `state.py escalate --reason "..."` (or `state.py raise-gate`) could log a structured reason and read more naturally, but adds API surface for little gain.
trigger: Revisit if supervised UI grows a need for richer transition flows.
resolution: Lifecycle transitions already work via `state set project.json state=<enum>`, and the escalation reason is already captured in a devlog entry. A named op (escalate/raise-gate) just merges two calls into one nicer command -- sugar that adds API surface for little gain (FU-4 own assessment). Reopen only if a supervised write-surface (deferred indefinitely today) creates real demand.

title: No read-side query helper in `state.py` (e.g., `state.py query devlog.jsonl --where 'contracts != []'`)
context: The assembler (Phase 1.3) exposes pre-formatted views: `--section devlog --phase N` gives a bulleted phase tail, `--section status` an orientation snapshot. Ad-hoc queries still fall back to `jq`. Per ARCH §2 / §10, the assembler intentionally does not absorb general-purpose queries.
trigger: Phase 2 pilot reveals a repeated query pattern worth absorbing into `--section`.
resolution: Largely obviated. Common read patterns are now first-class control CLI projections (i2c status / devlog --phase N / decisions --phase N / escalation / logs) -- none existed when FU-14 was filed. Arbitrary ad-hoc queries stay jq by design (ARCH section 2 / section 10: do not absorb general-purpose queries). Trigger obsolete -- FU-39 removed the operator --section modes. File fresh if a specific repeated query pattern proves worth its own projection.

title: `Module Contract` section is hard-required when `phases.json[current].module` is set
context: Per ARCH §11.1 / §4.1, the assembler exits 1 if a phase declares a `module` field but no `ARCH_<module>.md` file exists. This is strict by spec — useful for catching missing contracts early — and the FU-32 Δ4 ARCH-authoring discipline (per `ref/SPEC_architecture.md`) now codifies pre-authoring as the standard: every module's ARCH is written during architecture-phase work *before* any PLAN runs on that phase. **Original CC pilot (2026-06-05)** workaround (pre-author `ARCH_resolver.md` at bootstrap) is now the documented norm rather than a workaround.
trigger: Only revisit if a future workflow genuinely needs to plan against an unwritten ARCH (e.g., research/spike phases). For now the strictness is correct.
resolution: Resolved as correct-by-design: the hard-require catches missing module contracts early, and the FU-32 Delta-4 ARCH-authoring discipline makes pre-authoring each module ARCH the standard (was a workaround, now the norm). The strictness stands -- no change wanted. Reopen only for a workflow that must plan against an unwritten ARCH (research/spike phases).

title: Available Modules ARCHITECTURE.md fallback is naive
context: When the adapter's `## Available Modules` section is placeholder-only, the assembler grabs `## Implementation Sequence` from `ARCHITECTURE.md` verbatim and surfaces its body. If projects use richer Implementation Sequence tables (extra columns, longer prose), the rendered Available Modules section will be noisy.
trigger: Phase 2 / 3 pilots show real-world Implementation Sequence tables overflow the section. Tighten the fallback to extract only module names, or document a project convention for the fallback shape.

title: Assembler tests slow on Windows network share
context: `tests/test_assemble_context.py` runs in ~60s on `\\192.168.0.50\shared\...`. Primary cost: `TempProject(with_framework=True)` copies the full `instructions/` directory and WORKER_SPEC + both adapters per test invocation.
trigger: If iteration cost becomes painful, refactor `TempProject` to copy only what each test class needs (most renderer tests don't read instructions), or cache the framework copy per pytest session. Not a correctness issue.
resolution: Cached the fixture + adapter files locally once per process; tests copytree from the local cache instead of the Samba share on every test. test_assemble_context.py: ~60s -> ~20s (110 tests, ~3x). Follow-up shipped (df8698e): extracted the cache into shared tests/_fixtures.py and routed all 9 fixture-copying suites through it; full suite ~260s -> ~194s. Fully resolved.

title: Autonomous PLAN via ARCH-driven step decomposition (deltas 1-4 shipped)
context: After CC Phase 4 EXECUTE shipped supervised (commit `97e9ea4`), the meta-question surfaced: i2c's autonomous loop runs EXECUTE/REVIEW/CLOSE cleanly, but PLAN's step-breakdown step still requires human authoring because ARCH files aren't constrained enough to drive mechanical step decomposition. e2e solves this via a two-step workflow (pre-arch design separately, autonomous batch implementation); i2c lacks the ARCH-authoring discipline and the safety-net escalation triggers that make autonomous PLAN safe. Five deltas identified — see the progress log below for current state and the Δ5 spec.
trigger: Continue with CC Phase 5+ ARCH authoring against the new template; Δ5 follows once the template is validated.
resolution: Delivered. Deltas 1-4 shipped 2026-06-09; validated on clankercourts (13 Pattern-A ARCHes, Phases 2-14 autonomous). Delta5 (ARCH-completeness precondition) declined as specced -- no occurrence, and the original spec would false-halt successful phases (ARCH_resolver/validator ran fine without Escalation-Triggers). File-fresh-if-needed: (a) a `## Phasing`-only soft check, only for undisciplined external/migrated ARCHes; (b) Pattern-B autonomous validation, exercised when diplomat/phosphene migrate.

title: Centralize commits in the deterministic runner (worker stops running git)
context: Commits are model-owned today: EXECUTE commits code (`phase.step:`), CLOSE (`close.md` step 10) commits docs + `.state/`; the runner and `state_machine.py` never committed (`state_machine` is read-only by design, so the committer is the runner). **Increment 1 shipped:** the runner commits `.state/`+telemetry after a successful CLOSE — only a post-worker committer can capture the close tail (close devlog / audit_boundary / the runner-authored telemetry row all land *after* the worker's own commit). **Direction:** move *all* commits to the runner — the worker edits files + writes `.state/` via `i2c state`; the runner commits (code as `N.M:` using the devlog `summary` as the body; `.state/`+telemetry at the boundary). This **resolves FU-8** (the runner enforces the `phase.step:` format that recovery's `commit_exists_step_pending` depends on) and removes worker-git hazards (interactive-hang, wrong scope, forgotten commits). Commits are scoped (`git commit -- .state`) so operator WIP is untouched.
trigger: Migrate EXECUTE/REVIEW deliberately after the CLOSE increment proves out; requires rewriting `execute.md`/`close.md` to drop worker git + a golden regen.
resolution: Inc 3 shipped: runner now commits REVIEW fix-ups and CLOSE docs (phase-level) alongside the .state/ tail, joining the EXECUTE commit. Worker git fully removed from execute/review/close instructions + WORKER_SPEC + adapters; goldens regenerated; 164 tests green. Resolves FU-8 (runner enforces the phase.step:/phase: commit-message format).

title: execute.md commit-format suggestion (`phase.step: title`) is not enforced anywhere
context: The prose says "default commit message format `phase.step: short title`" but nothing validates it. A pre-commit hook or a `state.py complete --validate-commit-msg` check could enforce. **Superseded by FU-40** — centralizing commits in the runner enforces the format by construction.
trigger: Phase 2 pilot reveals workers drift from the format and downstream tooling (codexbot `/diff <phase>`, waymark commit-by-phase view) needs consistency.
resolution: Resolved by FU-40: the deterministic runner now commits all worker output (EXECUTE/REVIEW/CLOSE) and enforces the phase.step: / phase: commit-message format, so the format is no longer merely a suggestion. Downstream tooling can rely on it.

title: Refine regime in execute.md uses `step: null` for devlog entries
context: The schema allows `step: null` and the prose recommends it for Refine iterations. But there's no constraint that ties a Refine entry to *which* iteration (no iteration counter field). The commit message carries it (`14.iter3:`) but the structured data doesn't.
trigger: Phase 2 pilot does enough Refine work that iteration-by-iteration analytics matter. Add `iteration: int` optional field to `devlog_entry.schema.json`.
resolution: Folded into D-refine-8: the `devlog_entry` schema change for refine rows also adds the optional `iteration: int` field, so a null-step entry (Refine-regime or refine-tier) can name its iteration. Tracked there; telemetry.jsonl already covers the quantitative per-iteration analytics.

title: Production-incident anecdotes in WORKER_SPEC §3 are e2e-vintage
context: Per D-prose-8 the Codex 105k-char and Claude 5-3 incidents stay verbatim — they have pedagogical value. But once i2c has its own incidents, those should be added or substituted to keep the pedagogy current. **2026-06-21:** the public de-Meta pass dropped the explicit `(e2e)` / `state_machine.sh` labels (the anecdotes now read as neutral "A Codex/Claude iteration"); the refresh-with-i2c-native-incidents ask still stands.
trigger: i2c accumulates 2+ documented loop-discipline failures of its own. Add a refresh pass to WORKER_SPEC §3.

title: i2c's `CODEX.md` and `CLAUDE.md` adapters lacked an inline `## Output Contract` section; codex skips the 5-line exit signal as a result
context: The e2e template (`templates/CODEX_worker.md` line 136) and diplomat (`CODEX.md` line 188) both ship an explicit `## Output Contract` section that reads *"End every invocation with exactly these five lines — no additional text after"* plus the 5-line example and an exit-code table. i2c's adapters only reference `WORKER_SPEC.md` (which contains the contract) without inlining it. Claude is robust enough to follow the contract from the reference alone; codex is not. **CC Phase 3 iter 15 (2026-06-07):** first codex-on-i2c production run after the runner gained `--backend codex` support. Codex completed step 3.4 correctly — commit `f7620cc`, 228/228 tests pass, `state.py` writes for steps.json and devlog.jsonl landed coherently — but emitted prose-only output with no 5-line EXIT signal. Runner correctly reported `exit=2 "signal missing or malformed"` even though the work was substantively successful. **Partial fix applied (2026-06-07):** ported the e2e Output Contract section verbatim (with i2c-specific wording — `.state/project.json` rather than `DEVPLAN`) into `i2c/CODEX.md`, `i2c/CLAUDE.md`, `clankercourts/CODEX.md`, `clankercourts/CLAUDE.md`. Section sits between `## Runner Info` and `## Mode`. Re-firing the next codex iter on clankercourts validates the fix. **Surface reduction (FU-7, 2026-06-12):** contract is now 2 lines instead of 5; codex iter 65 (2026-06-11) showed the partial fix is necessary-but-not-sufficient (still skipped the block). A smaller block has less surface to skip but doesn't address the root cause (codex defaulting to conversational tail without the EXIT/REASON pair).
trigger: **Remaining work for full resolution:** (a) once i2c grows a `templates/` directory for bootstrap adapters (today the top-level CODEX.md / CLAUDE.md double as both reference and template), make sure the templates include the Output Contract section so every new i2c project ships with it; (b) consider whether claude adapters genuinely need it — claude historically follows the contract from WORKER_SPEC alone, but inlining is belt-and-suspenders and harmless. The CC pilot's own adapters have been patched, so this FU stays open until the template-layer fix lands.

title: Worker-facing prose drifts toward threat-framing instead of reason-first
context: Style principle, surfaced 2026-06-10 while rewriting the decisions-phase rule. **Pattern:** `field — does X for purpose Y. Read from Z.` Sourcing second, purpose first. **Anti-pattern:** imperative + reasoning-from-error + operator-context remediation + escape-hatch enumeration. The worker doesn't act on what-happens-if-broken or on the operator's recovery procedure; including that text adds prompt budget and shifts processing tone defensively. Worked example: `**Always include phase: ...** -- Decisions without phase do not appear ...; the operator has to back-fill later.` (3 lines) → `phase: <current phase id> -- marks the decision as belonging to this phase, so it appears in the phase audit (...). Read from Project State.` (2 lines, same info).
trigger: Apply the lens at next touch of `WORKER_SPEC.md`, `instructions/{plan,execute,review,close}.md`, or adapter Tool Rules. Not urgent enough for a dedicated pass; opportunistic cleanup. Likely candidates: `close.md` (many "do X so that Y" lines with Y as operator context), `plan.md` step 2.5 escalation-triggers table's Resolution column.

title: Dead-surface audit as a refine survey call (detect -> file dead-surface FUs)
context: A refine-tier survey, NOT bespoke boundary tooling: rides the refine machinery (Proposal B) rather than a standalone command / doctor check / inline-close hook. Detection is automatable (vulture or AST for unused imports/functions/vars; grep/import-graph for CLI flags, env vars, assembler --section modes, tools imported only by tests, schema fields written-but-never-read); the cut-or-keep decision is NOT (load-bearing via dynamic dispatch / public API / planned use -- a false positive means auto-deleting live code, high blast radius), so deletion stays human-gated. Distinct from diagnose (recovery tier: reactive, iteration-targeted, reads .state/ + loop logs, feeds reconcile deterministically): this is proactive, whole-tree, reads source, feeds the fu backlog by judgment. Per D-refine-7 they stay separate lifecycles but may share the finding/proposal reporting shape. Pays off: FU-7, STOP_BEFORE_REVIEW, STEP_BUDGET removals were all ad-hoc-audit finds.
trigger: Depends on Proposal B growing a survey/propose facet (a refine call that files FUs, mirroring the execute-a-FU mode). Then dead-surface survey = a refine call that runs the detector (vulture + grep, a tool the refine worker uses) and files dead-surface FUs; each executes via normal refine dispatch, one commit, human-gated. Invoke opportunistically (a phase/module boundary is natural), scoped to the module just closed to avoid big-bang. Supersedes the earlier three placement options (standalone command / doctor / inline-close). Spec: DESIGN_refine_v1 Proposal B survey mode + D-refine-7.

title: Templates assume `.claude/commands/` autoloads in Devmate; project-level `.llms/commands/` also doesn't get picked up in the workflows seen so far — operator-global `~/.llms/commands/` is the only reliable surface
context: `templates/README.md` states "Devmate / Claude Code picks up the project's `.claude/commands/` automatically — no extra configuration step." True for Claude Code, false for Devmate. Devmate's `agent_customization` skill documents `.llms/commands/` as the project-level convention. **CC pilot (2026-06-05/06) found both don't work in practice for the current Devmate session:** the operator's Devmate session is reading commands from `C:\Users\myeluashvili\.llms\commands\` only; neither `p:\shared\clankercourts\.claude\commands\*.md` nor `p:\shared\clankercourts\.llms\commands\*.md` showed up in the personal_context skills list. Possible causes: network-share path not scanned, workspace-root mismatch, requires Devmate restart to pick up new project-level commands, or project-level scanning not actually implemented for this Devmate build. **Workaround applied:** copied the 5 i2c slash commands to `~/.llms/commands/i2c-*.md` (operator-global with `i2c-` prefix). Now `/i2c-phase-plan`, `/i2c-cold-start`, etc. are available in any Devmate session; global `/phase-plan` continues to call e2e (Diplomat workflow unaffected). The commands shell out to `python tools/...` so they only do useful work inside an i2c project root; elsewhere they fail with a clear error.
trigger: Address before next i2c bootstrap: **(a)** update templates to ship the `i2c-` prefixed commands at both `templates/.claude/commands/` (for Claude Code) and `templates/.llms/commands/` (for Devmate at project-level if/when that works), AND document a manual copy-to-global step for Devmate users (`xcopy templates\.llms\commands\* %USERPROFILE%\.llms\commands\`); **(b)** investigate whether Devmate project-level `.llms/commands/` actually loads — may be a config / workspace setup question, or a network-share limitation. If (b) confirms project-level works under some setup, document the prerequisites.
resolution: Investigated (part b): Devmate loads slash commands ONLY from global ~/.llms/commands/ — project-level .claude/commands/ AND .llms/commands/ do not load (only .llms/rules/ does); Claude Code (which auto-loaded .claude) is retired. Resolution: refreshed the canonical i2c-* command set (i2c CLI; incl. Build tests-action fork, review acceptance-suite integrity check, audit_boundary gate) and ship it under templates/.llms/commands/ as the copy-to-global source; documented the xcopy-to-global bootstrap in templates/README (supersedes D-prose-4's per-project premise in practice); built the working set in ~/.llms/commands/i2c-*; removed stale per-project copies from clankercourts.

title: Fleet refine-tier adoption: roll i2c fu backlog to toolkit + diplomat (clankercourts pilot done)
context: Proposal A (i2c fu) was dogfooded on i2c and piloted on clankercourts (2026-07-05, commit 1fd85f7): 17 open items -> .state/followups.json, closed history frozen to archive/, FOLLOWUPS.md reduced to a pointer. Remaining: (a) toolkit -- extract the 6 open LLM-client gap items G-5..G-10 from VALIDATION_NOTES.md into i2c fu (leave the rest; it is interface verification, not a backlog); (b) diplomat (selective) -- import only the flat parked items (NEXT_STEPS.md project-only residual + papers/WORK_SEQUENCING.md section 8 icebox); LEAVE WORK_SEQUENCING (structured publication plan), RESEARCH_NOTES, and experiments/TUNING_LOG* in place. Template: fu add per open item; freeze closed to archive/followups_closed.md; reduce prose tracker to a pointer; verify (fu list/render + migrate --check); commit. Decisions: i2c fu is the general deferred-work backlog (not refine-only); execution stays manual until the Proposal B loop ships. Plan: .llms/plans/fleet_fu_adoption.plan.md.
trigger: Next fleet-maintenance touch; toolkit is quick (6 items), diplomat needs selective judgment.

title: Complete rate-limit exit-3 signal: codex detection + bot /batch handling
context: Runner exit-3 for a backend rate-limit/infra error shipped for claude (detected structurally via is_error + api_error_status; 429 = rate limit; committed 912fdc8). Two follow-ups remain: (a) codex backend detection -- detect_rate_limit() returns None for codex today; (b) the i2c bot /batch loop should recognize runner exit=3 and halt-and-report 'backend rate-limited, retry after reset' instead of treating it as a generic phase failure. Origin: clankercourts 2026-07-06 phase-16 claude usage-cap stumble (iters 109-110). FINDING (2026-07-06, inspected clankercourts codex .jsonl): a healthy codex stream has only thread/turn/item .started/.completed events -- no error/failure event type observed in success. Content string-matching is UNSAFE -- '429'/'rate'/'Error' appear hundreds of times inside normal agent/code content, so a naive scan would false-positive exit-3 and lose good work. DECISION: do NOT wire codex blind; wait for a real codex rate-limit sample and match on a PROTOCOL-level anchor (a distinct error event, or the turn envelope / process rc). Note claude returns rc=0 with an is_error envelope, so codex's rc behavior on rate-limit must be verified from a sample, not assumed.
trigger: Capture a real codex rate-limit/quota .jsonl first (now more likely since execute/close route to codex), then wire detect_rate_limit()'s codex branch + the bot exit-3 handling. Grab the iteration_NNN.jsonl when it happens.

title: Hard CLOSE acceptance-suite integrity invariant (D-tests-4 part 2)
context: tests action v1 shipped soft integrity only: execute.md prohibits editing the frozen tests/acceptance/phase_<N>/ suite and review.md flags weakening as a Must-fix. The deterministic post-CLOSE invariant is deferred.
trigger: Benchmark-era. Needs a TESTS-commit marker (or suite digest) recorded in .state/ so the pure-.state invariants.py can verify the acceptance suite was unchanged since the N.tests: commit, plus git access + graceful skip on non-git fixtures.

title: Scope tests_pass oracle to the acceptance suite (Q-tests-3)
context: The increment-2 tests_pass telemetry field is only meaningful once [telemetry].test_cmd points at the frozen acceptance suite (tests/acceptance/phase_<N>/) rather than the whole/self-written suite. tests action v1 authors the suite but does not yet scope the oracle to it.
trigger: Benchmark-era: when wiring the clean per-phase oracle, point test_cmd (or a new default) at the acceptance dir so tests_pass grades the contract; keep the whole-suite run at CLOSE.
resolution: Oracle supports {phase} interpolation to scope tests_pass to tests/acceptance/phase_<N>; records interpolated tests_cmd; graceful-skips (None, not false-red) when the scoped suite dir is absent.

title: Supervised: fold acceptance-suite authoring into phase-plan command (tests §9)
context: tests action v1 ships the autonomous path only. In supervised mode one session performs every action, so there is no per-action backend to route to; the design folds test-authoring into the supervised phase-plan command as a distinct step (write the contract-derived acceptance suite after planning), NOT a separate phase-tests command, so the suite is still frozen before EXECUTE.
trigger: When the supervised command layer is next revised: add the acceptance-suite step to the phase-plan command.

title: Bootstrap doc: add explicit seed-phases.json step
context: README Bootstrap a new i2c project jumps from (i2c init seeds empty phases) straight to (i2c assemble --action plan --phase 1) but never says to append phase records. The assembler hard-requires a record for the current phase (assemble_context.py ~L702: phases.json must list current phase), so following the documented steps verbatim errors out. Add a step after fill-scaffolded-files to append one phases.json record per phase via i2c state append-record phases.json, then set the gate via i2c state set project.json phase=1 state=plan.
trigger: Standing up build-a-stew on the share: i2c assemble failed until phases.json was seeded by hand.
resolution: Fixed in README bootstrap: added an explicit seed-phases.json step and choose-pattern-at-init guidance (Pattern A sets module; Pattern B omits it), so following the steps verbatim no longer errors at first i2c assemble. Done alongside FU-48.

title: Bootstrap doc: phase module field is optional and requires ARCH_<module>.md
context: Bootstrap step 4 says author ARCH_<module>.md for each module that needs a contract, but does not state that setting the module field on a phase record makes ARCH_<module>.md mandatory (render_module_contract error_exit in assemble_context.py ~L757). Single-document Pattern B projects must omit module from phase records or assemble fails with (module contract missing). Document the module-optional rule plus Pattern B guidance in the bootstrap section.
trigger: build-a-stew (Pattern B) assemble failed with (module contract missing: ARCH_bootstrap.md); needed an init --force redo to drop the module field.
resolution: Upgraded and superseded by FU-48 : reclassified from doc-reconciliation to a bugfix because PLAN silently sets the phase module, which then hard-breaks single-document (Pattern B) assembles. Doc note still folded into the new FU.

title: PLAN silently sets phase module, breaking single-document (Pattern B) projects
context: During PLAN the worker writes module (and dependencies) onto the current phase record even for single-document projects that have no ARCH_<module>.md. The assembler then hard-requires ARCH_<module>.md for every following action (render_module_contract error_exit, assemble_context.py ~L757), so TESTS and EXECUTE fail at prompt assembly. Observed on build-a-stew: phases were seeded module-less, PLAN added module=bootstrap, then /batch exited exit=2 at the TESTS assemble (module contract missing: ARCH_bootstrap.md) with no iter-2 transcript. Fix options: (a) PLAN should not set module unless the project opts into per-module contracts or ARCH_<module>.md already exists; (b) auto-scaffold a stub ARCH_<module>.md when PLAN sets module; or (c) assembler degrades to ARCHITECTURE.md when module is set but no contract file exists. Upgrades FU-47 from a doc fix to a behavior fix.
trigger: build-a-stew autonomous /batch exited exit=2 at TESTS assembly: PLAN had set module=bootstrap but ARCH_bootstrap.md does not exist (Pattern B).
resolution: Fixed via explicit project.json.pattern flag (D-pattern-1). Schema adds optional pattern enum [A,B] (absent=A); assembler render_module_contract omits the module contract under pattern=B and ignores a stray module (no more exit=2); plan.md step 4 sets module only under Pattern A; i2c init --pattern stamps it; schema_version 2->3 no-op migration; Pattern A missing-file error now hints pattern=B. Verified: build-a-stew TESTS assembly now exits 0. 644 tests + smoke green.

title: Pattern B: load ARCHITECTURE.md as module-contract source in EXECUTE/CLOSE
context: In Pattern B (module absent) render_module_contract returns empty, so EXECUTE and CLOSE receive no architecture doc at all - ARCHITECTURE.md is assembled only for PLAN and REVIEW, while Pattern A gets ARCH_<module>.md in all five actions. Proposal: when project.json.pattern==B, use ARCHITECTURE.md as the module-contract source for EXECUTE/CLOSE (and possibly TESTS), loaded via the real path with correct first-h2 extraction, and skipped in PLAN/REVIEW to avoid double-loading the doc already present there. Open question: does this help or just bloat the EXECUTE prompt, given the frozen acceptance suite already encodes the contract? Rejected the ARCH_ITECTURE.md filename-pun (module=ITECTURE) as too fragile/surprising.
trigger: Surfaced while planning FU-48 (explicit project.json.pattern flag). Blocked on FU-48 landing - the pattern flag is the prerequisite signal. Decide on merits once a Pattern B project (build-a-stew) has run EXECUTE/CLOSE and we can see whether missing arch context actually hurts.

title: Sanctioned acceptance-oracle correction path (fix a buggy test is not weakening)
context: The tests action freezes an acceptance suite as an independent oracle; D-tests-4 makes integrity soft (EXECUTE must not weaken it; REVIEW flags weakening as a Must-fix). But a genuinely BUGGY oracle needs legitimate correction, which is indistinguishable from weakening under the current model. build-a-stew Phase 3 step 2 (iter 25) burned 11.4M input tokens over 23 minutes fighting a wrong test (over-broad /low|medium|high/ matcher; a non-deterministic 30-iteration Tab scan in jsdom), attempted anti-patterns three times, then escalated and required a human steer (D-22) to authorize changing the frozen suite; D-23 cascaded one Must-fix into 14 test-query rewrites. Need a sanctioned oracle-correction lane: EXECUTE/REVIEW may fix a demonstrably broken acceptance test with a recorded justification (decision), kept distinct from weakening, and the CLOSE integrity check (FU-43) should treat a justified correction differently from an unexplained diff. Benchmark-critical: oracle integrity is the linchpin the benchmark rests on.
trigger: Surfaced by the build-a-stew greenfield run; needed before the benchmark replay trusts tests_pass as an oracle.

title: TESTS action: contract-coverage checklist + oracle anti-pattern guidance
context: The frozen acceptance suite is only a real oracle if it encodes the contract AND avoids fragile assertions; build-a-stew exposed both gaps. Contract-coverage: Phase 2 had two REVIEW escalations (iters 18 and 19) for contract drift the suite never checked - StewBuild dropped fields, and removeIngredient silently no-opped instead of throwing the ARCHITECTURE-guaranteed typed error - so EXECUTE passed tests while violating the contract and REVIEW was the only catch. Anti-patterns: TESTS authored fragile oracles (jsdom keyboard assumptions, an over-broad /low|medium|high/ matcher, a non-deterministic 30-iteration Tab scan) that cost 11.4M tokens at iter 25. Add to instructions/tests.md: (a) a contract-coverage checklist enumerating every ARCHITECTURE/ARCH guarantee including error modes and field-retention, asserting each; (b) an oracle anti-pattern list: no non-deterministic scans, scope matchers to the exact element, avoid environment-specific (jsdom) behavioral assumptions.
trigger: build-a-stew Phase 2 contract-drift escalations plus the Phase 3 iter-25 fragile-test blowup.
resolution: Added contract-coverage checklist (assert every guarantee incl. error modes + field-retention) and oracle anti-pattern list to instructions/tests.md; goldens regenerated. 701 tests green.

title: Oracle telemetry: tests_pass null across a full run; seed test_cmd + include typecheck/build
context: All 59 telemetry rows of build-a-stew (the flagship greenfield run) have tests_pass=null and tests_cmd=null: the benchmark linchpin metric recorded nothing across a complete project, making build-a-stew unusable as a benchmark substrate. Causes: (1) the telemetry test_cmd was never configured - i2c init / scaffold does not seed it and nothing warns when it is unset on an autonomous run; (2) the oracle excludes typecheck/build even when wired - Phase 4 iter 45 had green vitest but a broken tsc (replaceAll needs ES2021), so tests_pass would be a false green for a compiled project; (3) the suite could not run in the autonomous environment at all (NTFS node_modules and tsc-shim permission). Fixes: seed or prompt for test_cmd at init; for typed/compiled projects include the typecheck and build in the oracle, not just the test runner; warn when test_cmd is unset so tests_pass=null is not silent. Extends FU-44, which assumes test_cmd is set and only needs scoping to the acceptance directory.
trigger: build-a-stew telemetry review: tests_pass null for all 59 iterations.
resolution: Runner warns when [telemetry].test_cmd unset (no longer silent null); i2c.toml template recommends test_cmd + documents typecheck/build chaining; config.py docstring fixed.

title: Per-iteration runaway guard (token/time ceiling) in the runner
context: The max-budget-usd flag caps the run series, not a single iteration, and codex iterations are uncosted (cost_usd null), so a single runaway iteration has nothing to stop it but the worker three-strikes rule. build-a-stew iter 25 consumed 11.4M input tokens over 23 minutes on codex fighting a buggy test before it escalated. Add a per-iteration ceiling (token count and/or wall-clock) that aborts a single invocation cleanly with a distinct exit (mirroring the exit-3 rate-limit path), so a runaway cannot silently burn a large budget - especially important for codex where the dollar cap cannot fire.
trigger: build-a-stew iter 25: a single iteration burned 11.4M tokens over 23 minutes.
resolution: Per-iteration wall-clock ceiling: worker subprocess killed past max_iteration_seconds -> exit 4 (nothing landed). ON by default 1200s (data: >p99 of real iterations), tunable via [run].max_iteration_seconds + --max-iteration-seconds; 0 disables. In-flight wall-clock only (tokens unobservable until process end).

title: i2c refine on followups-only repos (self-dogfooding, D-refine-3)
context: run_refine currently requires a standard .state/ (project.json) because assemble_context.find_project_root and telemetry regime/leaf derivation assume it. To let i2c dogfood its OWN backlog via i2c refine (a followups-only repo, no phase machine), extend find_project_root to also anchor on followups.json (mirror control._find_followups_root), make build_context load project/phases/steps optionally for --action refine, and make telemetry degrade gracefully without project.json.

title: run_iteration rate-limit (exit 3) telemetry row silently dropped
context: run_iteration._emit_telemetry(3) on the rate-limit path records exit_code=3, but telemetry_entry.schema.json exit_code enum is {0,2,null}, so append_validated_jsonl raises and the best-effort wrapper drops the row -> every rate-limited iteration produces zero telemetry (invisible to cost/quota analysis). run_refine.py was fixed to emit exit_code=None on this path (surfaced during Proposal B review); run_iteration.py:932 still has the original bug. Apply the same fix (pass None) for consistency.
trigger: Surfaced by the Proposal B code review. Fix next time run_iteration telemetry is touched.
resolution: Fixed with FU-53: telemetry exit_code enum widened to {0,2,3,4,null}, so exit-3 (rate-limit) rows no longer fail schema validation and get silently dropped.
